bottom_line: In SHIFT, ivabradine vs placebo reduced the primary composite endpoint of cardiovascular death or hospital admission for worsening heart failure (HR 0.82 [0.75–0.90]).
implications: Based on the reported SHIFT results, ivabradine on top of standard therapy reduced the composite of cardiovascular death or hospital admission for worsening heart failure (HR 0.82 [0.75–0.90]) and reduced hospital admission for worsening heart failure (HR 0.74 [0.66–0.83]), but did not show a statistically significant reduction in all-cause mortality (HR 0.90 [0.80–1.02], p = 0.092).

major_points.text: SHIFT was a multinational, event-driven, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group trial in moderate to severe heart failure with left-ventricular systolic dysfunction.
major_points.quote: SHIFT was designed as a multinational, event-driven, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group clinical trial including patients with moderate to severe heart failure and left-ventricular systolic dysfunction [14].

major_points.text: Key population features included LVEF ≤35%, resting heart rate ≥70 bpm in sinus rhythm, and prior hospital admission for decompensated heart failure within 12 months.
major_points.quote: A total of 6558 adults with stable but symptomatic chronic heart failure (left-ventricular ejection fraction [LVEF] ≤35%), a resting heart rate ≥70 bpm in sinus-rhythm, and admission to hospital for decompensated heart failure within the previous 12 months

major_points.text: The primary endpoint was cardiovascular death or hospitalisation for worsening heart failure.
major_points.quote: The primary composite endpoint was cardiovascular death or hospitalisation for worsening heart failure.

major_points.text: A total of 6558 patients were randomised; 6505 were analysed after a mean follow-up of 23 months.
major_points.quote: A total of 6558 patients were randomised and 6505 patients were analysed after a mean follow-up of 23 months.

major_points.text: All-cause mortality was not statistically significantly reduced with ivabradine.
Hospital admission for worsening heart failure was reduced with ivabradine.

major_points.text: Bradycardia leading to permanent study withdrawal occurred more often with ivabradine than placebo.
major_points.quote: bradycardia leading to permanent study withdrawal occurred in 48 patients (1%) taking ivabradine, compared to 10 patients (<1%) receiving placebo [14].

major_points.text: Visual disturbances occurred more often with ivabradine than placebo.
major_points.quote: visual disturbances occurred in 89 patients (3%) randomised to ivabradine versus 17 patients (<1%) receiving placebo [14].

criticisms.text: The lack of benefit on all-cause mortality was noted as disappointing.
criticisms.quote: The lack of benefit on all-cause mortality is certainly disappointing.

criticisms.text: A very low use of device therapy was noted, despite guideline qualification for ICD; only 3% received ICD and 1% received cardiac resynchronisation therapy.
criticisms.quote: According to clinical guidelines, all patients in SHIFT would have qualified for an implantable cardioverter defibrillator (ICD), but in fact only 3% of the patients received such a device and only 1% received cardiac resyn- chronisation therapy [14].

criticisms.text: This low device use was stated as likely related to the recruitment strategy (66% eastern Europe, no USA centres, 14% western Europe).
criticisms.quote: This is likely to be related to the recruitment strategy in SHIFT: Two thirds of the patients were recruited in eastern Europe (66%) with no centres in the USA, and only 14% of the patients originated from western Europe [14].

criticisms.text: SHIFT was not designed to show an improvement in all-cause mortality because it was powered for the composite primary endpoint.
criticisms.quote: However, SHIFT was not designed to show an improvement in all-cause mortality, since the study was powered for the compos- ite primary endpoint of cardiovascular death or hospi- talisation for worsening heart failure.

criticisms.text: In patients receiving at least 50% of target beta-blocker dosage, there was no significant effect on the primary endpoint.
criticisms.quote: In patients re- ceiving at least 50% of the target beta-blocker dosage, there was no significant effect on the primary endpoint

criticisms.text: The results of SHIFT were described as questionable in patients in NYHA functional class I or IV.
criticisms.quote: Since the majority of the patients in SHIFT were in NYHA functional class II (49%) or III (50%), the results of SHIFT are questionable in patients in NYHA func- tional class I or IV.
